LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyRenown: The colony is known among the peoples for what its people did, and each of them for their own deeds.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyRenown_Tip: The colony's name among the peoples, read from everything its people did that the world saw, the living and the gone: contests won at feasts, marriages with other peoples, wards fostered well, seasons abroad as the colony's youth, envoy or hostage, truces sworn as its speaker; what the peoples remember of them by name (a raiders' camp broken, fighting beside their fighters, trade at their posts, prisoners freed, their wounded tended, and the wrongs); the colony's names for them, years in office and the Empire's titles; notables who think well of them; and the colony's own oaths kept and broken. A deed counts in full for a year, then a tenth less each season down to three tenths. At 10 its name is known in a town nearby, at 30 across the region, at 60 among every people within reach; at -15 it is known for the wrong things. What most of it came from is what it is known for: fighters, healers, hosts, traders, makers or the faithful. Each colonist is known by name for their own deeds the same way, shown on their card ("the one who won the wrestling at the feast with the Lenlia") and spoken of by visitors whose people know it. Nothing is spent. Notables think up to 15 better of a renowned colony's people (up to 10 worse of an infamous one's), good words for them count up to half again, matches with them are offered and accepted up to twice as readily, and what the colony is known for draws the world's events of that kind: challengers to fighters, the sick and the hurt to healers, guests to hosts, the far market to traders, work remembered to makers, pilgrims to the faithful, up to three quarters more often; one of its people known by name for something draws those events a quarter more, and the champion's challenge goes to a colonist known by name as a fighter more often than not; a feast's guests answer a colony known for hosting up to three tenths more readily. Off: nothing is told, read or tipped.
